Put .env.local in the Clincoo Project .gitignore

Ignoring only .env is not enough. An .env.* pattern keeps local keys on the machine.

This article is available in: Indonesian · English

A .env.local file often slips into Git because .gitignore only lists .env. Local keys then travel with every teammate clone.

Ignore .env and .env.*, and keep an exception for .env.example. That pattern protects a public sample without exporting machine values.

GitHub can detect secrets after they are pushed, but a .gitignore rule is cheaper than an emergency key rotation.

After adding the pattern, check git status. A file that was already tracked must be untracked or it still goes out.

On a Clincoo project, separate local editor values from variables that belong on the deploy host. Do not treat them as the same list.
